title: 9 of 13 dependencies use unpinned caret ranges — potential for breaking changes on install
evidence: framer-motion ^12.42.2, typescript ^5, @playwright/test ^1.61.1, tailwindcss ^4, @tailwindcss/postcss ^4, eslint ^9, @types/node ^20, @types/react ^19, @types/react-dom ^19. Only next (16.2.10), react (19.2.4), react-dom (19.2.4), and eslint-config-next (16.2.10) are exactly pinned.
rationale: Caret ranges allow minor/patch updates. For a hackathon demo deployed once and frozen, this is extremely low risk — the lockfile pins exact versions. If using npm ci (which reads lockfile), versions are locked regardless of package.json ranges. Only npm install (no lockfile) or fresh npm install with deleted lockfile would be affected.
fix_guidance: Low priority for hackathon. For production: change ^ to exact versions and use Dependabot for automated updates. Currently: ensure CI uses npm ci, not npm install.

title: No known vulnerable transitive dependencies — dependency tree is clean
evidence: package-lock.json contains no axios, node-fetch (packages with high CVE rates). sharp is present as optional dependency of next — currently no known CVEs for sharp 0.34.x per Snyk/OSV. All packages are mainstream with active maintenance. The dependency tree is shallow — only 4 runtime deps means minimal transitive attack surface.
rationale: The extremely lean dependency count (4 runtime deps) is a security strength. No known CVEs in the current lockfile state.
fix_guidance: No action needed. Run npm audit periodically for new CVEs. Consider adding npm audit to CI pipeline.

title: All listed dependencies are used — react-dom is Next.js peer, not direct import
evidence: Grep across src/ for imports: next (5 files), react (6 files), framer-motion (5 files), react-dom (0 files). react-dom is a required Next.js peer dependency — Next.js uses it internally for SSR/hydration. All dev deps verified used: typescript (tsc), @playwright/test (spec files), tailwindcss (config), @tailwindcss/postcss (postcss config), eslint/eslint-config-next (eslint.config.mjs), @types/* (tsconfig).
rationale: react-dom not directly imported is normal for Next.js apps — Next imports it internally. All other deps are actively used. No dead weight.
fix_guidance: Optionally add a comment in package.json noting react-dom is a Next.js peer requirement to prevent accidental removal.

title: All dependencies use permissive licenses — no GPL/AGPL copyleft issues
evidence: next/react/react-dom: MIT. framer-motion: MIT. typescript: Apache-2.0. tailwindcss: MIT. eslint: MIT. @playwright/test: Apache-2.0. Only copyleft-adjacent licenses found: LGPL-3.0-or-later on @img/sharp-libvips platform binaries (optional, only applies if bundled into redistributable — not applicable for web app). CC-BY-4.0 on caniuse-lite (dev, build-time only).
rationale: The LGPL-3.0 on libvips platform binaries is irrelevant — these are optional sharp dependencies for native image processing, not used in Alter Ego. CC-BY-4.0 requires attribution if caniuse-lite data is exposed, which it isn't (build-time only). All direct dependencies are MIT/Apache-2.0 — commercially safe.
fix_guidance: No action needed. If the project is ever redistributed as a packaged binary (Electron/desktop app), review sharp's LGPL dependency. For web-only deployment: no issue.

title: All dependencies are mainstream with no supply chain red flags
evidence: All 13 dependencies are well-known, high-download-count packages: next (Vercel, 1M+ weekly downloads), react (Meta, 20M+), framer-motion (2M+), tailwindcss (6M+), eslint (30M+), typescript (40M+), @playwright/test (Microsoft, 2M+). No packages with recent ownership changes, low download counts, suspicious names, or typosquatting patterns. All GitHub repos are actively maintained. The onchainos system dependency (not in package.json) is a legitimate OKX product.
rationale: Extremely low supply chain risk. Using only the most popular, well-audited packages in the JavaScript ecosystem. The 2-day hackathon timeline means no exotic or untested dependencies were introduced.
fix_guidance: No action needed. This is best practice for hackathon projects — use mainstream dependencies only.
